problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=2$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=1+2(x-2)+2(x-2)^{2}+\frac{4}{3}(x-2)^{3}+\frac{2}{3}(x-2)^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{‴}(2)?$

feedback.problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{(4)}(0)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The coefficient of ${x}^{4}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{(4)}(0)}{4!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{(4)}(0)}{4!} & =-\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{{f}^{(4)}(0)}{24} & =-\frac{1}{4} \\ {f}^{(4)}(0) & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
